Rw.bar_b_note: A clean, appealing elder with readable face and eyes, but the soft toy-like animated-film styling is a notch away from the naturalistic creature bar and the shipping-game finish.

Cd.bar_b_note: B's panel is legible and on-direction (blue-grey translucent, pale border), but it is a plain text list with little iconography, teal or gold accent and keyboard rather than controller glyphs, so it is not at shipping-UI finish.

Az.bar_b_note: B's aftermaths (freed cage, fallen banners, smoke plume) tell the story, but blurry flat ground, sparse scatter and boxy fortifications sink both sides well below Palworld density and Valheim light.

Jq.bar_b_note: A dense HUD over the bottom third, a dominant ally body and thin outline-ring tells with flat flash discs keep the fight from reading like Palworld's physical, world-integrated combat.

Mx.bar_b_note: A's fur boar is on the naturalistic track but its blotchy gold pattern, detached shadow in faint mid and roughly trainer-height scale fall short; B's smooth clay body with green moss decals reads as a toy, off the owner's style bar.

Zz.bar_b_note: The timber-and-stone village with lit windows and a castle at the end of the road is the closest to the key art, but the empty road, uniform grass verges and a night-rain grade that turns pale grey daylight keep it short of Valheim-class mood and Palworld density.

top_changes.change: Replace the blurry flat ground and uniform grass verges in Meadows (Az sites, Zz road, Jq arena) with clustered grass, wildflower and dirt variation, grove edges and scattered village props/villagers, and fix the night-rain grade so it reads as night

Rework the combat presentation: slim and move the HUD off the bottom third, frame or scale the ally so it never covers the opponent, and replace outline rings and flat flash discs with physical effects (dust, stones, sparks) and distinct hurt/move poses
Rebuild creature models to the owner's naturalistic bar (real fur/hide, coherent pattern, rim-lit) and above the 1.80 m trainer in scale, replacing the clay-toy boar look
